properties.statement:
AN OPEN PR'S EXPORT GOES STALE WHILE ITS BADGE STAYS GREEN, AND MERGING IT WOULD SUBTRACT DESIGN. Measured on reflow2's own repo, 2026-08-16, on THREE PRs at once — not a hypothetical, and not caused by anything anyone did wrong.

MEASURED, per PR, against `origin/main`:

    #190  export 63 nodes BEHIND main   intended to add 9   — all 9 ALREADY IN MAIN
    #191  export 59 nodes BEHIND main   intended to add 13  — all 13 ALREADY IN MAIN
    #194  export 56 nodes BEHIND main   intended to add 16  — all 16 ALREADY IN MAIN

All three were green on both CI jobs. #194 read `MERGEABLE`.

⭐ THE MECHANISM IS THE SHARED STORE, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. The design graph does not branch with git (`dec:multi-writer-architecture`), so a later session's export from the same store CARRIED EVERY EARLIER BRANCH'S GRAPH WRITES INTO MAIN. Each PR's design content therefore arrived in main WITHOUT that PR being merged. What was left on the branch was a document that could only subtract — `req:stale-seat-knows`'s prediction arriving in practice: a stale export is a COMPLETE document, so it merges cleanly and the missing work simply vanishes.

⚠️ THE HALF THAT MAKES IT DANGEROUS: nothing on the PR says so. The gate runs against the BRANCH's export and its own artifact checksums, so it passes; the branch is internally coherent. The subtraction is only visible by comparing the branch's export against MAIN, which no check does. A reviewer sees green, mergeable, and a diff of one JSON file.

⇒ THE CHECK, cheap and reusable — TWO questions, and the second is the one that decides:

    1. Does this PR's export ADD anything main lacks?
         set(branch nodes) - set(main nodes)          -> 0 means it can only subtract
    2. Are the nodes it INTENDED to add already in main?
         set(branch nodes) - set(merge-base nodes), then test each against main

When (1) is 0 and (2) is all-present, the PR's design half is ALREADY DELIVERED and the export is pure liability. #190 held nothing else, so it was CLOSED rather than merged — refreshing its export would have left an empty PR. #191 and #194 held real code, so each was rebased with `git checkout --ours docs/design/reflow2.json`, its artifact checksums re-accepted against its OWN existing ChangeEvent in main, and re-exported once.

📌 AND THE TRAP INSIDE THE REPAIR: those three PRs were GREEN because their stale exports carried their own artifact checksums. Restoring main's export makes them go RED on DRIFT immediately — which is correct, and must be fixed by re-accepting, never by keeping the stale export that was hiding it.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how long a PR can sit before this becomes true (all three were under 24 hours old), and whether anything could detect it automatically — the comparison needs main, and the gate deliberately only reads the committed export in front of it.
